items.title: Gold rings or rights? The patriarchal underpinnings of Tamil Nadu’s Thaimaman scheme
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government’s recent announcement of the Thaimaman Thanga Mothiram (TTM) (literally translates to Maternal Uncle’s Gold Ring scheme) – a one-gram gold ring to be given to babies born in government hospitals – needs to be evaluated through a gender lens. The scheme also raises the question of what the role of the state in welfare is and what its desirable role should be. The nomenclature and the narrative around the TTM scheme in particular reinforce the image of a patriarchal state that sees itself as protecting and caring for its citizens through its largesse, rather than one that represents people and pledges to carry forward the rights enshrined in the Constitution. Tamil Nadu is known for its welfare programmes – many of them progressive – setting up strong state institutions that are a model for the rest of the country. It has been a pioneering state in providing entitlements such as school mid-day meals, which over time have expanded to include breakfast, cover children up to class 10, and serve eggs on all days of the week. The site is at Pattinapakkam, close to Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s residence. The government order issued on September 8 said three committees have been formed to expedite the project. One will select an architectural consultant, while the other two will finalise the preliminary and final building designs. The Public Works Department has been asked to submit a detailed project report and estimates within three months.
